question: Are there any EU-funded or -supported programmes operating in Ireland or elsewhere that fund trauma-informed support structures for students in schools? If operating in Ireland, what is their managing authority? If there are no such programmes in Ireland or elsewhere, will the Commission, in the context of future cohesion policy, look at funding such support structures?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.8.2025) While Member States remain responsible for the teaching content and the organisation of their education systems1, the EU plays a prominent and active role supporting, coordinating and supplementing the actions of Member States.

The Commission monitors and supports Member States’ education policies under the European Education Area (EEA) framework, the European Semester and through EU funds. The EEA promotes mental health and wellbeing at school2, essential to ensure quality education for all. For example, the European School Education Platform3 provides resources to help schools respond appropriately to trauma.

The European Regional Development Fund funds the PEACE PLUS4 programme that supports young people and community-based initiatives to address the trauma as a legacy of the troubles; operating in Northern Ireland and the border counties in Ireland.

Ireland, through Tusla5, was a key partner in the ‘Side by Side’6 project under the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values Programme, contributing to the development of integrated, trauma-informed child protection services across Europe.

Ireland is also currently implementing Phase II of the Barnahus model – a child-centred, multi-agency response to child sexual abuse—co-funded under the Technical Support Instrument7 project. Under the current Erasmus+ programme8, Irish organisations coordinate more than 80 projects addressing ‘physical and mental health, well-being’ in school education.

Erasmus+ projects can entail exchanging best practices, which may improve understanding of mental health issues, including trauma. The Erasmus+ teacher academies create European partnerships of teacher institutions, which can also inform teachers on trauma-related issues.
